clue.text: Confrontational, in the view of an expert

definitions.meaning: openly opposing someone, standing directly before them

definitions.text: in the view of an expert
definitions.meaning: positioned directly in front of a specialist, under their gaze

explanation.surface: Someone's argumentative stance is described as what a specialist would make of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads like an opinion ('in the view of an expert') but is a separate sense: being directly in someone's sight and presence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a direct confrontation and also being in the immediate presence and sight of another person.

clue.text: Hand and foot, one's restrained

indicators.note: restrained means the second piece is held within the first

parts.note: one's is read as 'one is'; with I for one that is I'S, written here as IS

explanation.surface: Someone is bound hand and foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', and 'restrained' says that piece is held inside the abbreviation for foot. 'Hand and foot' reads as one phrase, but only 'Hand' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed hand is the clenched form of the hand, so hand works as a broad synonym.

clue.text: Lemmy's card

definitions.meaning: Lemmy ___ is the surname of the hard-boiled detective in Peter Cheyney's novels
a card is an amusing, eccentric person

explanation.surface: A possession belonging to someone called Lemmy.
explanation.walkthrough: Lemmy Caution is the FBI agent hero of Peter Cheyney's thrillers and Godard's Alphaville.
explanation.definitionFit: A comical person can be called a card, and the detective's surname completes his name.

clue.text: In bezique, the dealer may be very helpful

definitions.meaning: in the card game bezique the dealer turns over a card that fixes the trump suit
an idiom for proving unexpectedly useful

explanation.surface: In a card game, the dealer can be a great help.
explanation.walkthrough: Bezique is a two-player card game; after dealing, the next card is turned up to set trumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to come through unexpectedly well, and literally describes revealing the trump suit in cards.

clue.text: Trimming coat with down

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur
down means below, lower

explanation.surface: A coat is trimmed with soft feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' suggests feathers, but it means lower.
explanation.definitionFit: A flounce or frill on a garment is a decorative edging.

clue.text: Fan can…

definitions.meaning: a fan is something that cools air
can is slang for prison, as is the other sense

explanation.surface: A fan is able to do something, to be continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots link to 7 down; 'can' is US slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that chills air is one sense, and the other is slang for jail.

clue.text: 29 mushrooms knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means the mushroom word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: ceps are a kind of edible wild mushroom (porcini)

explanation.surface: Some mushrooms get knocked back, like a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: '29' is the answer to 29 across, INVESTMENT; 'knocked back' turns CEPS round. The surface hints at drinking, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: A speculative purchase made in hope of profit is a form of financial outlay, so the shortened word suits the cross-referenced answer.

clue.text: …be an accessory to a criminal painter

indicators.note: criminal means the letters of painter are rearranged unlawfully

explanation.surface: Continuing 5: a fan can help a lawbreaking artist.
explanation.walkthrough: With 5 down the surface reads 'Fan can be an accessory to a criminal painter'.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate or belong to something is to be attached to it as a part.

clue.text: Capital horse for a duke

definitions.meaning: the Duke of Wellington's charger at Waterloo bore this name

explanation.surface: A fine horse fit for a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Wellington rode his chestnut stallion Copenhagen at Waterloo.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Danish capital city, and also the name of Wellington's famous warhorse.

clue.text: Here three quarters in a maul brought about a scoreless draw

definitions.text: Here three quarters in a maul brought about a scoreless draw

parts.words: Here three quarters in a maul brought about a scoreless draw
parts.note: 'Here' is clue number nine, and three is the figure that multiplied by itself makes nine; the rugby talk of a maul and a level, pointless score plays on 'square' as all level

explanation.surface: A rugby report: the three-quarter backs got caught in a maul and the game ended nil-nil.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own number, 9, is the key: three is the value that squared gives nine. The rugby picture (three-quarters are backs, a maul is a scrum-like tussle) supports 'square' as an all-square, level score.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is the value whose product with itself is nine, the clue's own number, which is the mathematical relation named.

clue.text: A little water fall

definitions.meaning: a tiny quantity of liquid, a single bead

explanation.surface: A modest waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a single small bead of liquid and a downward plunge.

clue.text: My stars come out, blazing

parts.note: workers who come out stop work, they strike
alight means on fire, blazing

explanation.surface: Stars appear in the sky, burning brightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My stars' is an exclamation of surprise, not about the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned exclamations of astonishment.

clue.text: Story accepted in this place

parts.note: a story can mean a lie, a fib
U stands for upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A tale is taken as true in this location.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class, socially accepted usage. 'In this' is padding before the definition, as in the phrase 'in lieu of'.
explanation.definitionFit: This borrowed French word means a stead or position, seen in the phrase meaning instead of.

clue.text: Serenity disturbed about a problem in sight

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the single letter a
disturbed means the letters of serenity are thrown out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Calmness is disturbed by some trouble in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges the letters of Serenity, and 'about' wraps that rearrangement round the A. 'sight' suggests a view, but here it means eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching eyes are a vision complaint, a difficulty with one's seeing.

clue.text: "Ma's led papa astray" — Seth's explanation for this projection?

indicators.note: astray means the letters of ma's led papa wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Seth, son of Adam and Eve, explains the throat lump: Mother led Father astray.
explanation.walkthrough: Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve; the joke is the forbidden fruit stuck in Adam's throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulge at the front of the throat is a prominence of the larynx.

clue.text: Alms given by the same people

parts.note: DO is short for ditto, meaning the same again
a people is a nation

explanation.surface: Charity provided by a single group.
explanation.walkthrough: DO, short for ditto, is a crossword staple for 'the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable gifts to the poor are a contribution, a gift of money or goods.

clue.text: Girl's turned brown

indicators.note: turned means the words for the girl and her verb are read backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name, and the 's stands for is: ANNE IS

explanation.surface: A girl has become brown, perhaps from the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', not a possessive: ANNE IS turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt or raw, this earth pigment is a reddish or yellowish brown colour.

clue.text: Tired of walking, the infantry get cross

parts.note: foot soldiers are the infantry, foot
sore can mean angry, cross

explanation.surface: Weary from marching, soldiers grow irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Having aching feet after a long march means being weary from walking.

clue.text: Harry, an artist wearing a plaid

indicators.note: wearing means the artist sits inside the garment

parts.note: a maud is a grey striped plaid worn in southern Scotland
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter is pictured dressed in a tartan wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry is the verb, to harass or raid, not a name. A MAUD is a Scottish shepherd's plaid.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to raid and plunder repeatedly, the same as going on a pillaging raid.

clue.text: Recall the rise of English Egyptologist

indicators.note: in a down clue, the rise of means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Howard Carter was the Egyptologist who found Tutankhamun's tomb

explanation.surface: Remembering how an English Egyptologist rose to fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the rise of' turns E + CARTER upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back over past events in memory is to recall them.

clue.text: Very lazy person put in order by the French

indicators.note: put in means the word for a person goes inside the word for an order

parts.note: a bid is an order or command
one can mean a person, as in 'one should'
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An idler is organised by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in order' looks like 'arrange', but 'put in' is the insertion and 'order' is BID.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means utterly indolent, idle to the very core.

clue.text: Adjust girl's attitude

parts.note: Di's: Di is a girl's name, with possessive 's
a pose is an attitude or posture

explanation.surface: Someone should change a girl's outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange or set in order is to adjust things.

clue.text: Scheme to circumvent the heartless section of press

indicators.note: to circumvent means the plan goes around the other piece

parts.note: a scheme is a plan

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A plot to get round a heartless part of the press.
explanation.walkthrough: The press is a printing press, not the newspapers: the platen presses paper onto the type.
explanation.definitionFit: The plate of a printing press that pushes the paper against the type is part of the machine.

clue.text: George put oil to a peculiar use

indicators.note: peculiar use means the letters of put oil to a are put to a strange new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone called George finds an odd use for oil.
explanation.walkthrough: George is RAF slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: George is the old airmen's nickname for an aircraft's automatic steering system.

clue.text: They say composer is a heel

indicators.note: they say signals that the composer's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian composer and pianist

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that a composer is a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' looks like a cad, but it is the verb a ship does when it leans over.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that heels leans to one side, which is the nautical sense of tilt.

clue.text: Part of mine has some lead, I think

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone thinks part of a mine contains a little lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal entrance passage is one part of a mining excavation.

clue.text: Design a tailless kite

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter of the word for kite is cut off

parts.note: kite is old RAF slang for an aircraft

explanation.surface: Someone designs a kite with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Kite is airmen's slang for an aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a scheme or layout drawn up in advance.

clue.text: Keep firm control

parts.note: firm means strong, solid
hold means control or grip

explanation.surface: An instruction to maintain a tight grip.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep is the noun: the main tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's keep is its fortified tower, a defensive fortress.

clue.text: Still of the night

definitions.meaning: ... so, nevertheless; also as in '... more'
the poetic word for ..., as in the eve of the day

explanation.surface: The calm of night-time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means 'yet' or 'still' as an intensifier, and is also the old poetic word for evening.

clue.text: Formally dressed for a siege

definitions.meaning: being ceremonially robed or invested with insignia
the surrounding of a town by a besieging force

explanation.surface: Wearing formal clothes for a blockade.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are old: investing someone is robing them, and investing a town is besieging it.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun once meant ceremonial robing and still means a military blockade of a stronghold.
